messages.subject: Faster Javascript Charting Libraries
parts:
I have a Shiny app which pulls in around 250k records, all of which are currently displayed in a ggplot line chart. This chart takes several seconds to display, after the rest of the app has finished loading.

About 18 months ago, I ran some tests with various javascript charting libraries, with R bindings - rCharts, Plotly, GoogleVis. They were all slower than ggplot to display chart results.

I decided I could live without the interactivity, in exchange for faster load times.

Over the last 12 months there has been a lot of advances in htmlwidgets for R and many more bindings to javascript libraries. I do currently use the very nice MetricsGraphics htmlwidgets (http://hrbrmstr.github.io/metricsgraphics/) interface to display scatter plots, for smaller, subsetted data.

Has anyone undertaken research as to whether some of these javascript library bindings are as fast or faster than ggplot? I'm guessing the answer is that they won't be faster, but as things have moved on since last I looked, I thought it worth asking.
